correctness.rationale: Exact coordinate and 153-pair metric reconstruction yields squared thresholds 1,2,3,4,5,6,8. At threshold one the complex is the once-subdivided octahedral graph with rank-seven H1. At squared threshold two, its complete 52-triangle decomposition is a triangulated cuboctahedral S2 with twelve free bridge triangles and eight additional octahedral 2-cells attached along nullhomotopic loops, hence a wedge of nine integral S2. At squared threshold three, the included 164-pair elementary free-face certificate removes all and only faces outside the same sphere; the induced integral degree-two persistence is split-surjective, so a primitive class survives. At thresholds four, five, six, complete vertex-toggle acyclic Morse matchings leave one vertex and no other critical cells (all 2484/29742/326574 Hasse arcs checked); threshold eight is a simplex. Reproduced output and included exact finite certificate support every critical lemma; no infinite assertion is inferred.

value.rationale: The complete Euclidean type-B3 root arrangement is a canonical two-length-shell symmetric point set, not an arbitrary slice. The new classification resolves its full integral topology across every distance transition, showing eight ephemeral short-shell degree-two cycles and one primitive persisting cuboctahedral boundary class. This phenomenon is not visible in the published long-root-only filtration and gives a natural benchmark for multi-shell root-sample persistence. The proof is structural (cell attachments and certified relative collapses), with limits to the stated fixed configuration.
